provenance: IBM AMLworld HI-Small. Altman et al., 'Realistic Synthetic Financial Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering Models', NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. Data: IBM Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering (AML), CDLA-Sharing-1.0. The corpus is entirely SYNTHETIC by IBM's own statement, generated by a multi-agent virtual world, not real customer data; what is real is the provenance, not the transactions. These are 8,192 rows of the held-out temporal test window, the last 30 percent of the transactions in time order (2022-09-07 14:55 to 2022-09-18 16:18), which the model was not fitted, tuned or calibrated on. Their 32 features are computed by the training script's own functions, exactly as it computes them for test rows: per-account aggregates causal, so each row sees only earlier transactions, and structural features from the rows before the test window. Checked when this file was built: the published graph scores AUPRC 0.1233 over all 1,523,504 rows of that window, the figure the registry records. Unlike the 8-feature PaySim sample this page uses for the FHE/MPC pipeline. Z-scored here by the StandardScaler published in the student's weights.json -- the same transform it was distilled under. These are the identical rows the gradient-boosting teacher's sample ships, so the two numbers on this page describe one row set.
split: the rows of finance_aml.gbm's sample, a draw from the held-out temporal test window, the last 30 percent of the transactions in time order, enriched to 2 percent laundering

input.layout: samples[i] is one transaction's 32 engineered features, z-scored

expected.note: 0.3132 on THESE rows, which is not the 0.0614 the registry records for this student. That figure is measured on all 1,523,504 rows of the test window at its real prevalence of 0.15%, about 1 in 656; these 8,192 rows come from the same window but are enriched to 2.0% laundering, because an unenriched draw of this size would hold about 12 positives and every metric on it would be noise. Rare-class F1 rises with prevalence, so the two differ by 5.1x and neither is wrong. Not even the ratio to the all-positive baseline survives it: 8.0x here against 20.2x on the whole window, so this sample checks that the browser reproduces the graph, not how good the student is. On these rows the student scores above its teacher (0.3132 against 0.2032) and over the whole window below it (0.0614 against 0.1519): enrichment rewards whichever model flags more, so the order of the two on this sample is not a ranking. Read this number against the 0.0393 baseline beside it, not against the registry's.
